Exclusive in @nature.com: A Canadian startup just completed first test of a method to stem emissions from thawing permafrost, placing woody mats on areas of rapid erosion. Researchers say the concept is promising, but faces steep obstacles to scaling up in the Arctic. 
www.nature.com/articles/d41...
posts.external_title: Woody ‘blankets’ are being deployed on Arctic permafrost to reduce carbon emissions
posts.external_description: A start-up company is testing whether stabilizing areas of rapidly eroding permafrost can prevent greenhouse-gas emissions.

posts.external_title: Observation of relativistic bond weakening in seaborgium hexacarbonyl - Nature
posts.external_description: Gas chromatography analysis of compounds formed by the superheavy element seaborgium shows that the hexacarbonyl complex Sg(CO)6 exhibits lower first bond dissociation energy than the lighter chemical homologue W(CO)6, owing to relativistic bond weakening effects.

posts.text: The European spiny water flea has reduced the diversity of native zooplankton by over 50%. A study finds it had been present in Canada for at least a century before first reports in the 1980s—and it may not have been introduced by humans. In PNAS: https://ow.ly/lkRK50ZV1nw
